title: Guarded-lane reservations and eviction-tempering for Dedicated capacity
creator: Lina K. Park
description: PRD to introduce a 'guarded lane' reservation mechanism and an eviction-tempering policy to reduce noisy preemption effects across tenant pools. This feature provides flexible short-term headroom, observable accounting for burst credits, and controlled eviction degradation to preserve tail latency for high-SLA tenants.
problem_statement: Customers using Dedicated capacity report transient tail-latency spikes when tenants are preempted or when opportunistic bursts evict active KV caches. Existing burst policies either allow abrupt preemption (causing client-visible errors and cache thrash) or are overly conservative (wasting reserved capacity). We need a mechanism that provides predictable short-term burst headroom while minimizing disruptive evictions and offering clear telemetry and billing for transient usage.
goals: Allow tenants to consume short-duration guarded headroom above their reservation up to a configurable credit limit
Minimize hard preemptions by introducing eviction-tempering that prefers graceful shedding (rate-limit, degrade quality) before evicting KV caches or killing workers
Expose per-tenant burst-ledger telemetry and accounting in Console for billing and debugging
Provide API primitives and Console controls to configure credit windows, tempering thresholds, and automatic rollback policies
non_goals: Replacing long-term reservation allocation logic (this is additive to existing reserve flows)
Implementing per-request machine-learning based eviction predictions (out of scope)
Deep integration with third-party billing systems during initial rollout (will provide export hooks)
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want tenants to be able to consume short bursts without causing noisy eviction cascades, so that my high-priority customers maintain SLAs under transient load
As an SRE, I want to see per-tenant burst ledger and eviction-temper metrics so I can triage capacity incidents
As a product manager, I want Console controls to set per-tenant guarded-lane caps and tempering aggressiveness so we can offer tiered burst SLAs
As an engineer, I want API hooks to query remaining burst credits and to request voluntary degrade modes (e.g., reduce max tokens) before being evicted
requirements: Credit ledger: track per-tenant burst credits (consumed and replenished) with 1s granularity and 30d retention in telemetry
Guarded headroom policy: allow configurable headroom % (e.g., +25%) and absolute token/sec caps for bursts

Tempering steps: a controlled sequence of actions before eviction: (1) signal client degrade (via response header/stream), (2) apply rate-limit, (3) reduce model quality via quantization/shorter context fallback, (4) cache eviction as last resort
Failover/rollback: automatic rollback to prior steady-state when burst credit is depleted or when preemption is unavoidable
Console UI: per-tenant panel with current credit balance, recent tempering events, and a slider to adjust tempering sensitivity
Telemetry: new metrics (burst_credit_balance, tempering_phase, evictions_avoided, temp_degrade_count) emitted to the platform metrics pipeline
SLA mapping: ability to map tempering profiles to customer tiers and include in billing exports
acceptance_criteria: A1: Guarded headroom can be configured per-tenant in Console and via API and persisted to tenant config store
A2: When a tenant exceeds reserved capacity but has burst credits, requests are routed into guarded lane and billed at defined rate; no immediate worker kills occur
A3: Tempering pipeline executes at most four ordered steps and logs the active phase in telemetry; evictions occur only after all prior phases have been attempted
A4: In canary (10% of traffic across 3 customers), observed eviction count reduces by >=60% compared to baseline over 72h under synthetic spike tests
A5: Console displays real-time burst credit balance, last 48h tempering events, and a history of prevented evictions; API responses include remaining_credit and tempering_phase
A6: Billing team can export burst usage per tenant via CSV for the billing window; numbers match ledger within 0.5% for sample tenants
A7: No user-visible 5xx spikes attributable to sudden worker preemption during the canary period; SLOs remain within existing targets
A8: Security review completed and design documented; feature toggles exist for emergency disablement
success_metrics: Evictions prevented: >=60% reduction in hard preemptions during spikes for canary tenants
Tail latency: 95th percentile request latency improves or remains flat for high-SLA tenants during transient bursts
Billing accuracy: ledger vs exported usage discrepancy <0.5% for sampled tenants
Customer ticket impact: reduce capacity-related SEV pages for canary customers by 80% within 30 days
Adoption: 25% of newly onboarded Dedicated tenants opt into guarded-lane within 90 days of GA
design_considerations: Tempering should be composable with existing preemption/fallback policies; it must respect tenant isolation and data plane boundaries
Ledger storage should be lightweight; use existing metrics DB with a compact time-series representation and a daily compaction job
Console UI must avoid exposing sensitive capacity details to lower-privileged users; tie visibility to RBAC scopes
Rolling back should be possible via a single feature flag per region and per-pool to protect against misconfiguration
api_changes: Add POST /v1/dedicated/{tenant_id}/request_degrade -> triggers voluntary degrade path and returns token_allowance
Extend existing reservation config model with guarded_headroom_percent and burst_credit_window_seconds
Add admin POST /v1/admin/pools/{pool_id}/tempering_override to set emergency tempering behavior
console_changes: Tenant detail page: new 'Guarded Lane' box showing balance, last tempering events, and toggle for profile selection
Pool settings: controls for default tempering sensitivity and default guarded headroom for new tenants
Alerting shortcuts: quick-create from tempering event to create incident runbooks
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics emitted: dedicated.burst.credit_balance, dedicated.tempering.phase, dedicated.evictions.attempted, dedicated.evictions.successful, dedicated.tempering.degrade_count
Alert: tempering_phase == eviction for >10min across >2 tenants in a pool -> P0 oncall
Dashboard: Guarded Lane overview showing active credits, recent prevented evictions, and per-pool tempering heatmap
Tracing: link tempering events to request traces for end-to-end latency debugging
dependencies: Runtime: implement ordered tempering pipeline and API hooks (ENG-51234)
Console: UI components for Ledger and event timeline (DES-22019)
Billing: CSV export schema and reconciliation (ENG-54102)
Telemetry: metrics ingestion and retention adjustments (SRE-33210)
RBAC: display restrictions for Console panels (ENG-49821)
risks: Over-promising: aggressive tempering may increase request latency if degrade steps reduce model quality too far
Billing disputes: customers may dispute burst accounting; need clear documentation and easy exports
Operational complexity: new knobs may be misconfigured leading to regional instability; require sane defaults and rollout gates
Telemetry load: high-cardinality ledger per-tenant may increase metrics ingestion costs; must cap resolution and aggregate
qa_plan: Unit, integration and chaos tests for the tempering pipeline; simulate thousands of concurrent burst events
Synthetic load tests comparing baseline vs guarded lane under defined spike profiles
End-to-end canary with 3 tenants across 2 regions for 14 days before wider rollout
Manual verification of Console UI and API endpoints; validate CSV billing export against ledger
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flags and admin-only APIs behind kill switch (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Internal dogfood and integration tests (4 weeks)
Phase 2: Controlled canary with 3 low-risk customers in US-west (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Expand canary to 20 customers and add EU region (4 weeks)
Phase 4: GA release with self-serve Console and billing export turned on (targeted release date)
Rollback: per-region feature flag; immediate disable reverts to baseline preemption behavior
notes: Coordinate with Sales to draft customer communication describing burst billing and opt-in terms
Prepare runbook additions for oncall explaining tempering phases and diagnostic commands
Consider a pilot commercial offering 'Guarded Lane Pro' with higher headroom and faster replenish rates
